summary: Hard if your agent must act on Instagram accounts you do not own: each instagram_business_* permission needs Advanced Access through Meta App Review, and the app must be connected to a business that has passed Business Verification before it can be published. Meta asks for a working, testable app, a privacy policy, a written reason and a screen recording for every permission. Meta says you should receive a decision within a week of submitting, but Business Verification and any rejected permissions add time. Creating the Business-type app and setting up Instagram business login takes about an hour, and in Development mode it works at once for accounts that have a role on the app. Only Instagram professional (business or creator) accounts can connect. Composio's managed Instagram app lets you skip most of this while prototyping, but it does not yet have every permission approved (comment management is missing).

difficulty.reason: Self-serve app creation, but every permission used by people without a role on the app needs App Review with screen recordings, plus Business Verification before publishing and an annual Data Use Checkup. No paid security audit, which keeps it below Gmail.

evidence.label: INFERRED
evidence.note: The requirements are sourced; the Hard rating is our judgement from them.

time.detail: Hands-on: About 1 hour to create the app and connect a test account; 1-2 days to prepare the App Review submission (privacy policy, recordings, a written reason per permission). Approval wait: Meta says you should receive a review decision within a week, so it can be only a day or two. The upper range of about 4 weeks adds Business Verification (no official duration found) and any resubmission after rejections.

evidence.label: INFERRED

requirements.name: Meta developer account and a Business-type app
requirements.detail: Choose use case Other, then app type Business; only Business apps can add the Instagram product. One person can be developer or admin on at most 15 apps.

requirements.name: Instagram professional account
requirements.detail: Business Login for Instagram gives access to Instagram professional account data. Personal accounts cannot be connected through this API.

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: The login doc talks about professional account data; the create-app page only says test accounts must be public. We read this as professional (business or creator) accounts only.

requirements.name: Business Verification
requirements.detail: Needed before you can publish the app (Live mode) and to get Advanced Access; not needed while only people with a role on the app connect in Development mode. App Review may also prompt for it.

requirements.name: Privacy policy URL, app icon, category and contact email
requirements.detail: Set in Settings > Basic. 1024x1024 icon without Meta trademarks. The privacy policy is shown to users at login.

requirements.name: Deauthorize callback and data deletion request URLs
requirements.detail: Meta's setup steps include adding a Deauthorize callback URL and a Data deletion request URL in Business login settings, alongside the OAuth redirect URIs. We did not confirm they are mandatory.

requirements.name: A testable app and screen recordings
requirements.detail: Meta tests the app itself using its own test accounts. Each permission needs a screen recording (1080p or better) showing a user granting it and the app using it. Set the app UI to English if possible; otherwise add captions. Audio is ignored. A permission without a recording is not approved.

scopes.name: instagram_business_basic
scopes.purpose: Basic profile and media of the professional account. Also needed to refresh long-lived tokens.

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: Meta does not use Google-style sensitivity tiers; we label these sensitive because each needs Advanced Access via App Review to be used by people without a role on the app.

scopes.name: instagram_business_manage_messages
scopes.purpose: Read and send direct messages. Requesting it automatically adds the Human Agent feature to the review.

steps.title: Decide whether you need your own app yet
steps.action: Composio has a managed Instagram app. Stay on it while prototyping. Switch to your own Meta app when you need your own name at login, permissions Composio does not request, or your own quota.
steps.expected_result: A decision: managed auth for now, or your own Meta app.

steps.title: List the permissions your agent needs
steps.action: Map each agent action to an instagram_business_* permission. Meta adds five permissions by default (basic, content_publish, manage_comments, manage_insights, manage_messages), described as required and recommended. Always keep instagram_business_basic, which is needed to refresh tokens; remove the others you will not use, since each one needs its own review evidence. Read each permission's Allowed Usage section.
steps.expected_result: A short permission list with one reason per permission for the human to review.

steps.title: Create a Business-type app and add Instagram
steps.action: In the App Dashboard click Create App, choose use case Other, app type Business, enter name and contact email. Add the Instagram product with API setup with Instagram login.
steps.expected_result: An app in Development mode with the Instagram product and an Instagram App ID and Instagram App Secret.

steps.title: Register Composio's callback in Business login settings
steps.action: In Instagram > API setup with Instagram login > Set up Instagram business login > Business login settings, add https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback as an OAuth redirect URI, plus your deauthorize callback and data deletion URLs. Check the saved list: the dashboard may add a trailing slash.
steps.expected_result: Redirect URI saved exactly as Composio sends it.

steps.title: Create a custom auth config in Composio
steps.action: In the Composio dashboard click Create Auth Config, pick Instagram, choose OAuth2, turn on Use your own developer credentials, paste the Instagram App ID and Instagram App Secret (not the Facebook app ID), set the same redirect URI and your permissions. Pass the auth config ID in your session's auth_configs. Some Composio toolkit defaults still use https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add; set the v3 callback explicitly in both the Meta app and the Composio auth config so they match exactly.
steps.expected_result: An auth config ID (ac_...) for Instagram.

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: Which Meta credentials Composio's Instagram toolkit expects (Instagram login vs Facebook login app ID) was not confirmed; check the field labels in the dashboard.

steps.title: Add testers and make a real API call per permission
steps.action: Add a public Instagram professional account as a tester under App Roles, connect it through a Composio Connect Link, and make at least one successful call with each permission. Calls must be within 30 days before you submit; they show up within 2 days.
steps.expected_result: The Request advanced access buttons become active in App Review > Permissions and Features.

steps.title: Complete Business Verification
steps.action: Connect the app to your business in App settings > Basic and complete Business Verification if not already done.
steps.expected_result: Business verified and linked to the app.

steps.title: Prepare the review material
steps.action: Draft a distinct usage description per permission (no copy and paste), test instructions for Meta's reviewers, and a recording script. The human records each screen recording (1080p or better, English UI if possible or captions otherwise, no audio needed) and publishes the privacy policy.
steps.expected_result: One description and one recording per permission, plus access instructions.

steps.title: Submit for App Review
steps.action: In App Review > Permissions and Features request advanced access for each permission, answer data handling questions, complete app settings and app verification details, add descriptions and recordings, then Submit for Review and accept the Platform Onboarding Terms.
steps.expected_result: Submission queued; Meta says you should receive a decision within a week.

steps.title: Switch the app to Live mode
steps.action: Only after approval, flip the app mode toggle to Live. In Live mode only approved permissions work, even for role users. Do the annual Data Use Checkup when asked.
steps.expected_result: Any Instagram professional account can connect through your Composio auth config.

nuances.detail: Login returns a short-lived token. Exchanging it server side gives a long-lived token valid for 60 days. It can be refreshed for another 60 days if it is at least 24 hours old, still valid, and the user granted instagram_business_basic. A token not refreshed within 60 days expires for good. The authorization code is valid for 1 hour, once.
There is no separate refresh token; the long-lived access token itself is refreshed at graph.instagram.com/refresh_access_token.

Development mode: only role users, test data visible only to them. Live mode: anyone, but only approved permissions, even for role users. Test posts made in Development mode become visible to everyone after going Live.
The redirect_uri must exactly match a saved OAuth redirect URI; the dashboard may add a trailing slash. Strip the trailing #_ from the returned code.
Facebook's discovery document lists no PKCE methods, but that document is for Facebook Login OIDC, not Instagram login. Whether Instagram login supports PKCE is not shown by our probes.

composio_note.detail: Instagram is in Composio's managed OAuth list (snapshot 2026-10-28). With the managed app your users log in to Composio's app, which Composio registers and maintains, so you can skip App Review and Business Verification while prototyping. You need your own Meta app for your own name at login, extra permissions or dedicated quota, and then you inherit the full App Review path above. Note that Meta Ads and Threads are bring-your-own only in Composio. Composio's managed Instagram app does not currently have every permission approved (comment management is missing as of this snapshot), so reply-to-comment flows need your own Meta app with that permission approved.
